A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ETTFS research framework. Their text, equations, figures and tables support comparison. All pages were inspected, including v2's Appendices A–F; v1 contains no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original MNIST and Fashion-MNIST classification results, training diagnostics, and initialization/pooling ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original classification, latency and ablation results across four datasets, including additional analyses in its appendices.

M1.justification: v2 adds weight normalization during training and a learnable affine transformation that is fused into synapses for inference (Section 3.3). It also replaces v1's Gaussian initializer with a uniform initializer having the same target variance. The renamed AMOS neuron retains the earlier firing-mask mechanism.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only MNIST and Fashion-MNIST. v2 retains these and adds CIFAR10 natural-image classification and DVS Gesture event-based recognition, substantially expanding the represented visual and temporal domains.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 expands the retained benchmark comparisons with methods including Mostafa, Comsa, Göl tz, Sakemi and STiDi-BP, and introduces conversion comparators such as TTFS clamped, LC-TTFS and T2FSNN. v1's STDBP is retained under the label Zhang et al.; it is not a new comparator.

E3.justification: The reported MNIST/Fashion-MNIST optimizer changes from Adam to AdamW, and the Fashion-MNIST CNN changes from SCNN1 to SCNN5. v2 adds a MNIST CNN evaluation, depth experiments spanning 5–11 layers, and test-set-averaged inference stopping time as a latency metric. The added datasets also receive distinct training protocols.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends the initialization/pooling analyses with normalization-induced distribution stability, separate normalization and affine ablations, and deeper-network tests. Figure 9 and Appendix Table 4 supply decay-function and gamma sweeps that v1 mentioned without reporting results. Appendix Table 5 extends component analyses across three datasets; v1's firing-rate-versus-iteration plot is not retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The plotted distribution variances describe network signals, and v2's moving-average training curves do not introduce uncertainty estimates across runs.

E6.justification: v1 Table I lists 99.2% MNIST accuracy, conflicting with 98.2% in its prose; v2 reports 98.67% for the MLP and 99.48% for the CNN. Fashion-MNIST CNN accuracy changes from 91.61% to 92.90% with a different architecture. New results include CIFAR10 at 90.56%, DVS Gesture at 95.83%, and extensive latency, decoding and component results in Tables 2–5. Method and protocol changes preclude treating these as uniform same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 revises the default-initialization premise and predicted current variance from 2/T in v1 Equation 12 to 1/(3T) in v2 Equation 13, and adds normalization/fusion formulas. The central one-spike variance derivation and target weight variance T/N remain, with much existing derivation material relocated to Appendix B.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion add normalization against training-time distribution shift as a core contribution. The claimed state-of-the-art coverage expands from MNIST/Fashion-MNIST to include CIFAR10 and DVS Gesture. Earlier claims about stable training, early firing and average pooling are retained.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of distribution drift after initialization and the representational constraint addressed by affine parameters. It discusses dataset-dependent decoding choices and vanishing-gradient risks from strong temporal decay. It also qualifies CIFAR10 comparisons against larger conversion models and explains propagation-mode and GPU limitations relevant to hardware efficiency.

D1.justification: Appendix Tables 6–7 newly document dataset-specific losses, epoch budgets, augmentation and detailed layer dimensions. v2 also explains affine initialization and inference fusion, but omits v1's explicit Atan surrogate and warm-up/cosine schedule description. Appendix E newly claims accompanying code, weights and logs; their availability cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises research positioning around neural coding and layer-by-layer versus step-by-step propagation. It adds relevant initialization, normalization and TTFS literature, and gives more specific limitations of earlier initialization approaches. v1's separate survey of SNN learning algorithms, including online training, is removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and substantial method and experiment prose are rewritten. Neuron background and derivations are reorganized into appendices, experiments receive separate accuracy/latency and component-analysis subsections, and terminology changes to AMOS and ETTFS-init. These changes substantially reshape the narrative beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: v2 merges the separate benchmark tables into a wide comparison table and adds latency, decoding, settings and architecture tables. It redesigns the overview and diagnostic plots, adds a propagation schematic, and redraws or relocates existing explanatory figures, including the neuron diagram moved to Appendix A. Typography and page layout also change throughout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for training stability and low latency through quantitative latency comparisons, deeper-network tests, and separate normalization/decoding ablations. CIFAR10 and DVS Gesture address v1's narrow empirical coverage, while the settings appendix improves implementation disclosure. These gains outweigh reporting defects, including Appendix C's linear/exponential decay mix-up and conflicting SCNN6 widths in Table 7, which still limit precision and reproducibility.
